units.unit: The student is working on a project about subdivided flats in Hong Kong and rent control.
The student needs to see the sources.
The student asks for documents on the basic situation of subdivided units.
The student wants raw numbers on how many households are in subdivided units and what they pay.
The student wants a tenant's own account.
The student wants numbers plus tenant accounts first.
The student needs supply evidence and stock figures.
The student needs the legal side and enforcement.
The student wants material on compensation claims from a hard cap.
The student wants material on inspection capacity.
The student recalls the sources as a lawyer's memo and a subcommittee note.
The memo should back up that a hard cap risks compensation claims.
An indexed per-square-foot band can be defended as rate-capping.
The subcommittee note should back up that enforcement is too thin.
Enforcement would miss tenants with no written agreement and newest arrivals.
The point is that enforcement can't protect the tail.
Legal compensation risk and enforcement capacity are both needed for the hard-cap objection.
